name: Social Security System
authority: RA 11199 ss.4(a)(9), 8(i), 9(a) and 18; SSS Circular 2024-006. Regular SS uses the first PHP20,000 monthly salary credit at 5% employee and 10% employer; excess to PHP35,000 belongs to SSS_MPF. Initial compulsory coverage extends through the 60th birthday. The first contribution liability date includes earlier employers and is independent of current registration. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/employees/ . Separation and retirement payments outside remuneration for services are excluded.

rules.refusal: SSS requires a birth date to determine statutory coverage.
SSS first contribution due date must be between birth and the assessment date.
SSS requires the first contribution due date, including earlier employers, to determine coverage.

assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + NIGHT_PREMIUM + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: SSS Mandatory Provident Fund (WISP)
authority: RA 11199 s.4(a)(2); SSS Circular 2024-006 II.B.2. Only a covered SSS member contributes to the Mandatory Provident Fund on salary credit above PHP20,000 through PHP35,000 at 5% employee and 10% employer. The Regular SS result establishes coverage, including the first-liability age test. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/pay-contribution/ .
assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + NIGHT_PREMIUM + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: Employees Compensation Programme premium
authority: Presidential Decree 626 as amended, Art.183 of the Labor Code — employer-only EC premium keyed to the SSS monthly salary credit Applied 2026-09-19 (2): RA 11199 s.8(i): compensation is remuneration for services; separation pay (Labor Code arts.298–299) and retirement pay (RA 7641) are paid for the ending of service, not for it, and are outside the contribution base.
assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + NIGHT_PREMIUM + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: PhilHealth
authority: Republic Act 11223 (Universal Health Care Act) s.10 with PhilHealth Circular 2019-0009 and Advisory 2025-0002 — one 5% premium on the monthly basic salary, floor PHP 10,000, ceiling PHP 100,000, then split: employee = truncate_cent(premium / 2), employer = premium - employee (the published employer table; a half-centavo premium such as basic 15,819 -> 790.95 gives 395.47 / 395.48, not 395.48 twice). The base is the BASIC line, which Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keeps whole against undertime, tardiness, leave without pay and absences (the ABSENCE and NO_PAY_LEAVE lines are not subtracted). Applied 2026-09-18: PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). Applied 2026-09-18: PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The base is the monthly basic salary whatever the pay frequency (`terms.monthly_basic`: a daily or hourly rate carried to the month by the person’s own factor). RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.30: where a domestic worker earns less than ₱5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium — the employee share is zero and the employer carries both.
assessed_on: person.terms.monthly_basic / period.month_factor

name: Pag-IBIG Fund (Home Development Mutual Fund)
authority: Republic Act 9679 s.7 with HDMF Circular 460 — 1%/2% employee, 2% employer, monthly compensation ceiling PHP 10,000. Applied 2026-09-18: HDMF Circular 460 keys the contribution off the contractual monthly compensation, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`, the standing allowances beside it). Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The base is the monthly basic salary whatever the pay frequency (`terms.monthly_basic`: a daily or hourly rate carried to the month by the person’s own factor). RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.30: where a domestic worker earns less than ₱5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium — the employee share is zero and the employer carries both.
assessed_on: person.terms.monthly_basic / period.month_factor - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: Withholding Tax on Compensation
authority: NIRC 1997 s.79 with s.24(A)(2)(a) as amended by RA 10963 (TRAIN), Revenue Regulations 11-2018 — revised withholding tax table effective 1 January 2023. The NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e) PHP 90,000 exemption for 13th-month pay is `annual_exempt(code('THIRTEENTH_MONTH_PAY'), year.earned.THIRTEENTH_MONTH_PAY, 90000.0)` in the formula. RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(d) as amended by RR 11-2018 — RR 29-2025 (issued 22 December 2025) is in force only from 6 January 2026, the next version — a rice subsidy of up to PHP 2,000 a month is a de minimis benefit outside compensation; the company's `meal` row is that subsidy (its sheet: "MEAL (RICE SUBSIDY)", with any excess booked as `allowance`), so the formula takes it out of the base up to PHP 30,000 a year — `annual_exempt(code('meal'), year.earned.meal, 30000.0)`, the monthly ceiling stated as its annual sum, exact for a level subsidy and reconciled by the year-end rung otherwise. The `bonus` allowance shares that ceiling and is not yet pooled with it (gap 105). The monthly and semi-monthly rungs relieve the SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG employee shares deducted in the same period (`produced.<code>.employee_this_period`, RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(B) as amended); only the year-end rung reads the year's shares. The SEMI-MONTHLY column (₱10,417 / 16,667 / 33,333 / 83,333 / 333,333; ₱937.50 / 4,270.70 / 16,770.70 / 91,770.70) governs a base paid in two instalments (`period.instalments == 2`); the MONTHLY column everything else. Applied 2026-09-18: RA 9504 (RR 11-2018): a statutory minimum-wage earner (basic at or below the region’s floor) is withheld on neither the basic wage, overtime, night shift differential nor holiday pay; the ₱90,000 exclusion is one pool across 13th-month pay and the bonus (NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e)); the de minimis meal allowance is exempt to 30% of the basic minimum wage (RR 29-2025); the MPF employee share relieves the taxable base beside the Regular SS share. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): NIRC s.32(B)(6)(a)–(b): retirement benefits under RA 7641 and separation pay for a cause beyond the employee’s control are excluded from gross income; s.24(A)(2) / RR 10-2008: a minimum wage earner’s statutory minimum wage, holiday pay, overtime pay and night shift differential are exempt (`person.wage_floor_pay`). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(13) / RR 10-2008: the exemption attaches to the pay for the days on which the employee is an MWE — the SMW is "the rate fixed by the RTWPB", which a wage order fixes from its effective date — so a month a wage order splits exempts the basic, overtime, holiday and night-differential pay of the days whose floor the rate is at or below and taxes the rest (`person.wage_floor_pay.<LINE>`: work-day lines by their date, the salary, leave and absence by the share of paid days). NCR September 2026: a ₱720 daily rate is above NCR-26’s ₱695 to 25 September (taxed) and at or below NCR-28’s ₱755 from 26 September (exempt). RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(d): the rice subsidy (the `meal` row) is de minimis to ₱2,000 a month, the excess taxable — a monthly figure, not a share of the annual minimum wage; the bonus is read once, through the 90,000 exemption, never also through the catalogue. The semi-monthly rung selector nets the MPF share with the SSS share. Applied 2026-09-19 (3): RR 11-2018 Annex E, the weekly column, for a payslip of a weekly-paying company (`period.instalments >= 4`: the month’s four or five weeks): nothing to ₱4,808; 15% over 4,808; 432.60 + 20% over 7,692; 1,971.20 + 25% over 15,385; 7,740.45 + 30% over 38,462; 42,355.65 + 35% over 153,846 — the annual schedule over fifty-two, as the Annex prints it. The daily column is for a payroll paid every day, a cadence the runs do not offer. Applied 2026-09-23 (engine audit): the pools are the scheme's parts, never a company's codes — a class counting toward `WTAX.SPECIAL` is 13th-month pay and other benefits inside the PHP 90,000 pool, one counting toward `WTAX.RICE` the de minimis rice subsidy (`earned_average('WTAX.RICE', 0, 1)`, `earned_monthly_excess('WTAX.RICE', …)`); the salary the period attributes to `MATERNITY_LEAVE` days (`person.period.leave_pay`) is outside the base (RA 11210 s.5; RMC 105-2019). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 3): this version covers 1–5 January 2026, before RR 29-2025 commenced, so the formula reads RR 11-2018’s ₱2,000 rice ceiling and 10 days of leave cash-out; the version of 6 January 2026 reads ₱2,500 and 12. RR 29-2025 s.3: in force fifteen days after publication on the BIR website (posted and stamped received 22 December 2025), i.e. 6 January 2026 — https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%2029-2025.pdf. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): NIRC s.22(E)-(G), s.24(A) and s.25(A)-(B): a citizen and a resident alien, and a non-resident alien engaged in trade or business (one in the Philippines more than 180 days in the calendar year is deemed engaged, s.25(A)(1)), are withheld on the graduated table; a non-resident alien not engaged is withheld 25% of the gross (s.25(B)). The classification is `terms.tax_residency` (RESIDENT / NON_RESIDENT / NON_RESIDENT_NETB); the Code states no default for an unrecorded status, so positive taxable pay with none recorded stops the run. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test needs the floor the wage order fixes for the person (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(13)); where the version states none for the person's region and employment type (a kasambahay outside NCR), positive taxable pay stops the run instead of treating the person as above the floor. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): every de minimis benefit of RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3) as amended by RR 11-2018 (and RR 4-2025 for uniforms and achievement awards, from 30 January 2025) is its own class and WTAX part, each exempt to its ceiling and its excess an ‘other benefit’ inside the ₱90,000 exclusion: uniform `UNIFORM` ₱7,000, actual medical assistance `MEDICAL` ₱10,000, achievement awards `AWARD` ₱10,000, Christmas/anniversary gifts `GIFT` ₱5,000, CBA and productivity benefits combined `CBA` ₱10,000 — each a year, read against the year’s earlier payments; laundry `LAUNDRY` ₱300 a calendar month (as the rice subsidy); medical cash to dependants `DEP_MEDICAL` ₱1,500 a semester (January–June, July–December), read against the semester’s earlier payments; the overtime/night-shift meal allowance `OT_MEAL` is exempt to 25% of the regional basic minimum wage for each date with overtime or night-shift work. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5, V): RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(j) caps the exemption, not the pay — the class pays the keyed amount whole; the formula exempts 25% × minimum_wage(region) × 12 ÷ 313 × `person.period.overtime_days` of the part and pools the excess with the other benefits inside the ₱90,000 exclusion (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph; RMC 50-2018). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5, Z): RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph (restated by RMC 50-2018) counts de minimis benefits paid in excess of their ceilings among the 'other benefits' of the PHP 90,000 pool for the whole year, so an earlier payslip's excess of the overtime/night-shift meal allowance over its daily ceiling is 'earned before' too: `earned_daily_excess('WTAX.OT_MEAL', share of the monthly floor a day)` sums, month by month, the part less that share of the minimum wage each payslip was calculated at (the wage order then in force) times its overtime or night days.

rules.refusal: Record tax residency on the employment terms before calculating Philippine withholding: resident (citizen or resident alien), non-resident alien engaged in trade or business (graduated rates, NIRC s.25(A)), or not engaged (25% final, s.25(B)). The Tax Code states no default for an unknown status.

This version states no minimum wage for this employee's region and employment type (e.g. a kasambahay outside a transcribed domestic-worker wage order), so minimum-wage-earner status (NIRC s.24(A)(2), RR 11-2018) cannot be determined. Record the applicable wage order in the version before calculating withholding.

name: Social Security System
authority: RA 11199 ss.4(a)(9), 8(i), 9(a) and 18; SSS Circular 2024-006. Regular SS uses the first PHP20,000 monthly salary credit at 5% employee and 10% employer; excess to PHP35,000 belongs to SSS_MPF. Initial compulsory coverage extends through the 60th birthday. The first contribution liability date includes earlier employers and is independent of current registration. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/employees/ . Separation and retirement payments outside remuneration for services are excluded.

rules.refusal: SSS requires a birth date to determine statutory coverage.
SSS first contribution due date must be between birth and the assessment date.
SSS requires the first contribution due date, including earlier employers, to determine coverage.

assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + NIGHT_PREMIUM + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: SSS Mandatory Provident Fund (WISP)
authority: RA 11199 s.4(a)(2); SSS Circular 2024-006 II.B.2. Only a covered SSS member contributes to the Mandatory Provident Fund on salary credit above PHP20,000 through PHP35,000 at 5% employee and 10% employer. The Regular SS result establishes coverage, including the first-liability age test. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/pay-contribution/ .
assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + NIGHT_PREMIUM + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

authority: Presidential Decree 626 as amended, Art.183 of the Labor Code — employer-only EC premium keyed to the SSS monthly salary credit Applied 2026-09-19 (2): RA 11199 s.8(i): compensation is remuneration for services; separation pay (Labor Code arts.298–299) and retirement pay (RA 7641) are paid for the ending of service, not for it, and are outside the contribution base.

name: PhilHealth
authority: Republic Act 11223 (Universal Health Care Act) s.10 with PhilHealth Circular 2019-0009 and Advisory 2025-0002 — one 5% premium on the monthly basic salary, floor PHP 10,000, ceiling PHP 100,000, then split: employee = truncate_cent(premium / 2), employer = premium - employee (the published employer table; a half-centavo premium such as basic 15,819 -> 790.95 gives 395.47 / 395.48, not 395.48 twice). The base is the BASIC line, which Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keeps whole against undertime, tardiness, leave without pay and absences (the ABSENCE and NO_PAY_LEAVE lines are not subtracted). Applied 2026-09-18: PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). Applied 2026-09-18: PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The base is the monthly basic salary whatever the pay frequency (`terms.monthly_basic`: a daily or hourly rate carried to the month by the person’s own factor). RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.30: where a domestic worker earns less than ₱5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium — the employee share is zero and the employer carries both.
assessed_on: person.terms.monthly_basic / period.month_factor

name: Pag-IBIG Fund (Home Development Mutual Fund)
authority: Republic Act 9679 s.7 with HDMF Circular 460 — 1%/2% employee, 2% employer, monthly compensation ceiling PHP 10,000. Applied 2026-09-18: HDMF Circular 460 keys the contribution off the contractual monthly compensation, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`, the standing allowances beside it). Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The base is the monthly basic salary whatever the pay frequency (`terms.monthly_basic`: a daily or hourly rate carried to the month by the person’s own factor). RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.30: where a domestic worker earns less than ₱5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium — the employee share is zero and the employer carries both.
assessed_on: person.terms.monthly_basic / period.month_factor - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: Withholding Tax on Compensation
authority: NIRC 1997 s.79 with s.24(A)(2)(a) as amended by RA 10963 (TRAIN), Revenue Regulations 11-2018 — revised withholding tax table effective 1 January 2023. The NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e) PHP 90,000 exemption for 13th-month pay is `annual_exempt(code('THIRTEENTH_MONTH_PAY'), year.earned.THIRTEENTH_MONTH_PAY, 90000.0)` in the formula. RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(d) as amended by RR 11-2018: a rice subsidy of up to PHP 2,000 a month is a de minimis benefit outside compensation; the company's `meal` row is that subsidy (its sheet: "MEAL (RICE SUBSIDY)"), so the formula takes it out of the base up to PHP 24,000 a year — `annual_exempt(code('meal'), year.earned.meal, 24000.0)`, the monthly ceiling stated as its annual sum. The `bonus` allowance shares that ceiling and is not yet pooled with it (gap 105). The monthly and semi-monthly rungs relieve the SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG employee shares deducted in the same period (`produced.<code>.employee_this_period`, RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(B) as amended); only the year-end rung reads the year's shares. The SEMI-MONTHLY column (₱10,417 / 16,667 / 33,333 / 83,333 / 333,333; ₱937.50 / 4,270.70 / 16,770.70 / 91,770.70) governs a base paid in two instalments (`period.instalments == 2`); the MONTHLY column everything else. Applied 2026-09-18: RA 9504 (RR 11-2018): a statutory minimum-wage earner (basic at or below the region’s floor) is withheld on neither the basic wage, overtime, night shift differential nor holiday pay; the ₱90,000 exclusion is one pool across 13th-month pay and the bonus (NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e)); the de minimis meal allowance is exempt to 30% of the basic minimum wage (RR 29-2025); the MPF employee share relieves the taxable base beside the Regular SS share. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): NIRC s.32(B)(6)(a)–(b): retirement benefits under RA 7641 and separation pay for a cause beyond the employee’s control are excluded from gross income; s.24(A)(2) / RR 10-2008: a minimum wage earner’s statutory minimum wage, holiday pay, overtime pay and night shift differential are exempt (`person.wage_floor_pay`). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(13) / RR 10-2008: the exemption attaches to the pay for the days on which the employee is an MWE — the SMW is "the rate fixed by the RTWPB", which a wage order fixes from its effective date — so a month a wage order splits exempts the basic, overtime, holiday and night-differential pay of the days whose floor the rate is at or below and taxes the rest (`person.wage_floor_pay.<LINE>`: work-day lines by their date, the salary, leave and absence by the share of paid days). NCR September 2026: a ₱720 daily rate is above NCR-26’s ₱695 to 25 September (taxed) and at or below NCR-28’s ₱755 from 26 September (exempt). RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(d): the rice subsidy (the `meal` row) is de minimis to ₱2,000 a month, the excess taxable — a monthly figure, not a share of the annual minimum wage; the bonus is read once, through the 90,000 exemption, never also through the catalogue. The semi-monthly rung selector nets the MPF share with the SSS share. Applied 2026-09-19 (3): RR 11-2018 Annex E, the weekly column, for a payslip of a weekly-paying company (`period.instalments >= 4`: the month’s four or five weeks): nothing to ₱4,808; 15% over 4,808; 432.60 + 20% over 7,692; 1,971.20 + 25% over 15,385; 7,740.45 + 30% over 38,462; 42,355.65 + 35% over 153,846 — the annual schedule over fifty-two, as the Annex prints it. The daily column is for a payroll paid every day, a cadence the runs do not offer. Applied 2026-09-23 (engine audit): the pools are the scheme's parts, never a company's codes — a class counting toward `WTAX.SPECIAL` is 13th-month pay and other benefits inside the PHP 90,000 pool, one counting toward `WTAX.RICE` the de minimis rice subsidy (`earned_average('WTAX.RICE', 0, 1)`, `earned_monthly_excess('WTAX.RICE', …)`); the salary the period attributes to `MATERNITY_LEAVE` days (`person.period.leave_pay`) is outside the base (RA 11210 s.5; RMC 105-2019). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): NIRC s.22(E)-(G), s.24(A) and s.25(A)-(B): a citizen and a resident alien, and a non-resident alien engaged in trade or business (one in the Philippines more than 180 days in the calendar year is deemed engaged, s.25(A)(1)), are withheld on the graduated table; a non-resident alien not engaged is withheld 25% of the gross (s.25(B)). The classification is `terms.tax_residency` (RESIDENT / NON_RESIDENT / NON_RESIDENT_NETB); the Code states no default for an unrecorded status, so positive taxable pay with none recorded stops the run. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test needs the floor the wage order fixes for the person (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(13)); where the version states none for the person's region and employment type (a kasambahay outside NCR), positive taxable pay stops the run instead of treating the person as above the floor. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): every de minimis benefit of RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3) as amended by RR 11-2018 (and RR 4-2025 for uniforms and achievement awards, from 30 January 2025) is its own class and WTAX part, each exempt to its ceiling and its excess an ‘other benefit’ inside the ₱90,000 exclusion: uniform `UNIFORM` ₱7,000, actual medical assistance `MEDICAL` ₱10,000, achievement awards `AWARD` ₱10,000, Christmas/anniversary gifts `GIFT` ₱5,000, CBA and productivity benefits combined `CBA` ₱10,000 — each a year, read against the year’s earlier payments; laundry `LAUNDRY` ₱300 a calendar month (as the rice subsidy); medical cash to dependants `DEP_MEDICAL` ₱1,500 a semester (January–June, July–December), read against the semester’s earlier payments; the overtime/night-shift meal allowance `OT_MEAL` is exempt to 25% of the regional basic minimum wage for each date with overtime or night-shift work. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5, V): RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(j) caps the exemption, not the pay — the class pays the keyed amount whole; the formula exempts 25% × minimum_wage(region) × 12 ÷ 313 × `person.period.overtime_days` of the part and pools the excess with the other benefits inside the ₱90,000 exclusion (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph; RMC 50-2018). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5, Z): RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph (restated by RMC 50-2018) counts de minimis benefits paid in excess of their ceilings among the 'other benefits' of the PHP 90,000 pool for the whole year, so an earlier payslip's excess of the overtime/night-shift meal allowance over its daily ceiling is 'earned before' too: `earned_daily_excess('WTAX.OT_MEAL', share of the monthly floor a day)` sums, month by month, the part less that share of the minimum wage each payslip was calculated at (the wage order then in force) times its overtime or night days.

rules.refusal: Record tax residency on the employment terms before calculating Philippine withholding: resident (citizen or resident alien), non-resident alien engaged in trade or business (graduated rates, NIRC s.25(A)), or not engaged (25% final, s.25(B)). The Tax Code states no default for an unknown status.

This version states no minimum wage for this employee's region and employment type (e.g. a kasambahay outside a transcribed domestic-worker wage order), so minimum-wage-earner status (NIRC s.24(A)(2), RR 11-2018) cannot be determined. Record the applicable wage order in the version before calculating withholding.

name: Social Security System
authority: RA 11199 ss.4(a)(9), 8(i), 9(a) and 18; SSS Circular 2024-006. Regular SS uses the first PHP20,000 monthly salary credit at 5% employee and 10% employer; excess to PHP35,000 belongs to SSS_MPF. Initial compulsory coverage extends through the 60th birthday. The first contribution liability date includes earlier employers and is independent of current registration. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/employees/ . Separation and retirement payments outside remuneration for services are excluded.

rules.refusal: SSS requires a birth date to determine statutory coverage.
SSS first contribution due date must be between birth and the assessment date.
SSS requires the first contribution due date, including earlier employers, to determine coverage.

assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + NIGHT_PREMIUM + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: SSS Mandatory Provident Fund (WISP)
authority: RA 11199 s.4(a)(2); SSS Circular 2024-006 II.B.2. Only a covered SSS member contributes to the Mandatory Provident Fund on salary credit above PHP20,000 through PHP35,000 at 5% employee and 10% employer. The Regular SS result establishes coverage, including the first-liability age test. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/pay-contribution/ .
assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + NIGHT_PREMIUM + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: Employees Compensation Programme premium
authority: Presidential Decree 626 as amended, Art.183 of the Labor Code — employer-only EC premium keyed to the SSS monthly salary credit Applied 2026-09-19 (2): RA 11199 s.8(i): compensation is remuneration for services; separation pay (Labor Code arts.298–299) and retirement pay (RA 7641) are paid for the ending of service, not for it, and are outside the contribution base.
assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + NIGHT_PREMIUM + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: PhilHealth
authority: Republic Act 11223 (Universal Health Care Act) s.10 with PhilHealth Circular 2019-0009 and Advisory 2025-0002 — one 5% premium on the monthly basic salary, floor PHP 10,000, ceiling PHP 100,000, then split: employee = truncate_cent(premium / 2), employer = premium - employee (the published employer table; a half-centavo premium such as basic 15,819 -> 790.95 gives 395.47 / 395.48, not 395.48 twice). The base is the BASIC line, which Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keeps whole against undertime, tardiness, leave without pay and absences (the ABSENCE and NO_PAY_LEAVE lines are not subtracted). Applied 2026-09-18: PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). Applied 2026-09-18: PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The base is the monthly basic salary whatever the pay frequency (`terms.monthly_basic`: a daily or hourly rate carried to the month by the person’s own factor). RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.30: where a domestic worker earns less than ₱5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium — the employee share is zero and the employer carries both.
assessed_on: person.terms.monthly_basic / period.month_factor

name: Pag-IBIG Fund (Home Development Mutual Fund)
authority: Republic Act 9679 s.7 with HDMF Circular 460 — 1%/2% employee, 2% employer, monthly compensation ceiling PHP 10,000. Applied 2026-09-18: HDMF Circular 460 keys the contribution off the contractual monthly compensation, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`, the standing allowances beside it). Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The base is the monthly basic salary whatever the pay frequency (`terms.monthly_basic`: a daily or hourly rate carried to the month by the person’s own factor). RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.30: where a domestic worker earns less than ₱5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium — the employee share is zero and the employer carries both.
assessed_on: person.terms.monthly_basic / period.month_factor - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: Withholding Tax on Compensation
authority: NIRC 1997 s.79 with s.24(A)(2)(a) as amended by RA 10963 (TRAIN), Revenue Regulations 11-2018 — revised withholding tax table effective 1 January 2023. The NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e) PHP 90,000 exemption for 13th-month pay is `annual_exempt(code('THIRTEENTH_MONTH_PAY'), year.earned.THIRTEENTH_MONTH_PAY, 90000.0)` in the formula. RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(d) as amended by RR 29-2025 (issued 22 December 2025, in force 6 January 2026): a rice subsidy of up to PHP 2,500 a month is a de minimis benefit outside compensation; the company's `meal` row is that subsidy (its sheet: "MEAL (RICE SUBSIDY)", with any excess booked as `allowance`), so the formula takes it out of the base up to PHP 30,000 a year — `annual_exempt(code('meal'), year.earned.meal, 30000.0)`, the monthly ceiling stated as its annual sum, exact for a level subsidy and reconciled by the year-end rung otherwise. The `bonus` allowance shares that ceiling and is not yet pooled with it (gap 105). The monthly and semi-monthly rungs relieve the SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG employee shares deducted in the same period (`produced.<code>.employee_this_period`, RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(B) as amended); only the year-end rung reads the year's shares. The SEMI-MONTHLY column (₱10,417 / 16,667 / 33,333 / 83,333 / 333,333; ₱937.50 / 4,270.70 / 16,770.70 / 91,770.70) governs a base paid in two instalments (`period.instalments == 2`); the MONTHLY column everything else. Applied 2026-09-18: RA 9504 (RR 11-2018): a statutory minimum-wage earner (basic at or below the region’s floor) is withheld on neither the basic wage, overtime, night shift differential nor holiday pay; the ₱90,000 exclusion is one pool across 13th-month pay and the bonus (NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e)); the de minimis meal allowance is exempt to 30% of the basic minimum wage (RR 29-2025); the MPF employee share relieves the taxable base beside the Regular SS share. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): NIRC s.32(B)(6)(a)–(b): retirement benefits under RA 7641 and separation pay for a cause beyond the employee’s control are excluded from gross income; s.24(A)(2) / RR 10-2008: a minimum wage earner’s statutory minimum wage, holiday pay, overtime pay and night shift differential are exempt (`person.wage_floor_pay`). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(13) / RR 10-2008: the exemption attaches to the pay for the days on which the employee is an MWE — the SMW is "the rate fixed by the RTWPB", which a wage order fixes from its effective date — so a month a wage order splits exempts the basic, overtime, holiday and night-differential pay of the days whose floor the rate is at or below and taxes the rest (`person.wage_floor_pay.<LINE>`: work-day lines by their date, the salary, leave and absence by the share of paid days). NCR September 2026: a ₱720 daily rate is above NCR-26’s ₱695 to 25 September (taxed) and at or below NCR-28’s ₱755 from 26 September (exempt). RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(d): the rice subsidy (the `meal` row) is de minimis to ₱2,000 a month, the excess taxable — a monthly figure, not a share of the annual minimum wage; the bonus is read once, through the 90,000 exemption, never also through the catalogue. The semi-monthly rung selector nets the MPF share with the SSS share. Applied 2026-09-19 (3): RR 11-2018 Annex E, the weekly column, for a payslip of a weekly-paying company (`period.instalments >= 4`: the month’s four or five weeks): nothing to ₱4,808; 15% over 4,808; 432.60 + 20% over 7,692; 1,971.20 + 25% over 15,385; 7,740.45 + 30% over 38,462; 42,355.65 + 35% over 153,846 — the annual schedule over fifty-two, as the Annex prints it. The daily column is for a payroll paid every day, a cadence the runs do not offer. Applied 2026-09-23 (engine audit): the pools are the scheme's parts, never a company's codes — a class counting toward `WTAX.SPECIAL` is 13th-month pay and other benefits inside the PHP 90,000 pool, one counting toward `WTAX.RICE` the de minimis rice subsidy (`earned_average('WTAX.RICE', 0, 1)`, `earned_monthly_excess('WTAX.RICE', …)`); the salary the period attributes to `MATERNITY_LEAVE` days (`person.period.leave_pay`) is outside the base (RA 11210 s.5; RMC 105-2019). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): NIRC s.22(E)-(G), s.24(A) and s.25(A)-(B): a citizen and a resident alien, and a non-resident alien engaged in trade or business (one in the Philippines more than 180 days in the calendar year is deemed engaged, s.25(A)(1)), are withheld on the graduated table; a non-resident alien not engaged is withheld 25% of the gross (s.25(B)). The classification is `terms.tax_residency` (RESIDENT / NON_RESIDENT / NON_RESIDENT_NETB); the Code states no default for an unrecorded status, so positive taxable pay with none recorded stops the run. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test needs the floor the wage order fixes for the person (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(13)); where the version states none for the person's region and employment type (a kasambahay outside NCR), positive taxable pay stops the run instead of treating the person as above the floor. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): every de minimis benefit of RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3) as amended by RR 29-2025 (issued 22 December 2025, in force 6 January 2026) is its own class and WTAX part, each exempt to its ceiling and its excess an ‘other benefit’ inside the ₱90,000 exclusion: uniform `UNIFORM` ₱8,000, actual medical assistance `MEDICAL` ₱12,000, achievement awards `AWARD` ₱12,000, Christmas/anniversary gifts `GIFT` ₱6,000, CBA and productivity benefits combined `CBA` ₱12,000 — each a year, read against the year’s earlier payments; laundry `LAUNDRY` ₱400 a calendar month (as the rice subsidy); medical cash to dependants `DEP_MEDICAL` ₱2,000 a semester (January–June, July–December), read against the semester’s earlier payments; the overtime/night-shift meal allowance `OT_MEAL` is exempt to 30% of the regional basic minimum wage for each date with overtime or night-shift work. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5, V): RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(j) caps the exemption, not the pay — the class pays the keyed amount whole; the formula exempts 30% × minimum_wage(region) × 12 ÷ 313 × `person.period.overtime_days` of the part and pools the excess with the other benefits inside the ₱90,000 exclusion (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph; RMC 50-2018). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5, Z): RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph (restated by RMC 50-2018) counts de minimis benefits paid in excess of their ceilings among the 'other benefits' of the PHP 90,000 pool for the whole year, so an earlier payslip's excess of the overtime/night-shift meal allowance over its daily ceiling is 'earned before' too: `earned_daily_excess('WTAX.OT_MEAL', share of the monthly floor a day)` sums, month by month, the part less that share of the minimum wage each payslip was calculated at (the wage order then in force) times its overtime or night days.

rules.refusal: Record tax residency on the employment terms before calculating Philippine withholding: resident (citizen or resident alien), non-resident alien engaged in trade or business (graduated rates, NIRC s.25(A)), or not engaged (25% final, s.25(B)). The Tax Code states no default for an unknown status.

This version states no minimum wage for this employee's region and employment type (e.g. a kasambahay outside a transcribed domestic-worker wage order), so minimum-wage-earner status (NIRC s.24(A)(2), RR 11-2018) cannot be determined. Record the applicable wage order in the version before calculating withholding.

name: Social Security System
authority: RA 11199 ss.4(a)(9), 8(i), 9(a) and 18; SSS Circular 2024-006. Regular SS uses the first PHP20,000 monthly salary credit at 5% employee and 10% employer; excess to PHP35,000 belongs to SSS_MPF. Initial compulsory coverage extends through the 60th birthday. The first contribution liability date includes earlier employers and is independent of current registration. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/employees/ . Separation and retirement payments outside remuneration for services are excluded.

rules.refusal: SSS requires a birth date to determine statutory coverage.
SSS first contribution due date must be between birth and the assessment date.
SSS requires the first contribution due date, including earlier employers, to determine coverage.

assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + NIGHT_PREMIUM + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: SSS Mandatory Provident Fund (WISP)
authority: RA 11199 s.4(a)(2); SSS Circular 2024-006 II.B.2. Only a covered SSS member contributes to the Mandatory Provident Fund on salary credit above PHP20,000 through PHP35,000 at 5% employee and 10% employer. The Regular SS result establishes coverage, including the first-liability age test. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/pay-contribution/ .
assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + NIGHT_PREMIUM + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: PhilHealth
authority: Republic Act 11223 (Universal Health Care Act) s.10 with PhilHealth Circular 2019-0009 and Advisory 2025-0002 — one 5% premium on the monthly basic salary, floor PHP 10,000, ceiling PHP 100,000, then split: employee = truncate_cent(premium / 2), employer = premium - employee (the published employer table; a half-centavo premium such as basic 15,819 -> 790.95 gives 395.47 / 395.48, not 395.48 twice). The base is the BASIC line, which Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keeps whole against undertime, tardiness, leave without pay and absences (the ABSENCE and NO_PAY_LEAVE lines are not subtracted). Applied 2026-09-18: PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). Applied 2026-09-18: PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The base is the monthly basic salary whatever the pay frequency (`terms.monthly_basic`: a daily or hourly rate carried to the month by the person’s own factor). RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.30: where a domestic worker earns less than ₱5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium — the employee share is zero and the employer carries both.

Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The base is the monthly basic salary whatever the pay frequency (`terms.monthly_basic`: a daily or hourly rate carried to the month by the person’s own factor). RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.30: where a domestic worker earns less than ₱5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium — the employee share is zero and the employer carries both.

name: Withholding Tax on Compensation
authority: NIRC 1997 s.79 with s.24(A)(2)(a) as amended by RA 10963 (TRAIN), Revenue Regulations 11-2018 — revised withholding tax table effective 1 January 2023. The NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e) PHP 90,000 exemption for 13th-month pay is `annual_exempt(code('THIRTEENTH_MONTH_PAY'), year.earned.THIRTEENTH_MONTH_PAY, 90000.0)` in the formula. RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(d) as amended by RR 29-2025 (issued 22 December 2025, in force 6 January 2026): a rice subsidy of up to PHP 2,500 a month is a de minimis benefit outside compensation; the company's `meal` row is that subsidy (its sheet: "MEAL (RICE SUBSIDY)", with any excess booked as `allowance`), so the formula takes it out of the base up to PHP 30,000 a year — `annual_exempt(code('meal'), year.earned.meal, 30000.0)`, the monthly ceiling stated as its annual sum, exact for a level subsidy and reconciled by the year-end rung otherwise. The `bonus` allowance shares that ceiling and is not yet pooled with it (gap 105). The monthly and semi-monthly rungs relieve the SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG employee shares deducted in the same period (`produced.<code>.employee_this_period`, RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(B) as amended); only the year-end rung reads the year's shares. The SEMI-MONTHLY column (₱10,417 / 16,667 / 33,333 / 83,333 / 333,333; ₱937.50 / 4,270.70 / 16,770.70 / 91,770.70) governs a base paid in two instalments (`period.instalments == 2`); the MONTHLY column everything else. Applied 2026-09-18: RA 9504 (RR 11-2018): a statutory minimum-wage earner (basic at or below the region’s floor) is withheld on neither the basic wage, overtime, night shift differential nor holiday pay; the ₱90,000 exclusion is one pool across 13th-month pay and the bonus (NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e)); the de minimis meal allowance is exempt to 30% of the basic minimum wage (RR 29-2025); the MPF employee share relieves the taxable base beside the Regular SS share. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): NIRC s.32(B)(6)(a)–(b): retirement benefits under RA 7641 and separation pay for a cause beyond the employee’s control are excluded from gross income; s.24(A)(2) / RR 10-2008: a minimum wage earner’s statutory minimum wage, holiday pay, overtime pay and night shift differential are exempt (`person.wage_floor_pay`). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(13) / RR 10-2008: the exemption attaches to the pay for the days on which the employee is an MWE — the SMW is "the rate fixed by the RTWPB", which a wage order fixes from its effective date — so a month a wage order splits exempts the basic, overtime, holiday and night-differential pay of the days whose floor the rate is at or below and taxes the rest (`person.wage_floor_pay.<LINE>`: work-day lines by their date, the salary, leave and absence by the share of paid days). NCR September 2026: a ₱720 daily rate is above NCR-26’s ₱695 to 25 September (taxed) and at or below NCR-28’s ₱755 from 26 September (exempt). RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(d): the rice subsidy (the `meal` row) is de minimis to ₱2,000 a month, the excess taxable — a monthly figure, not a share of the annual minimum wage; the bonus is read once, through the 90,000 exemption, never also through the catalogue. The semi-monthly rung selector nets the MPF share with the SSS share. Applied 2026-09-19 (3): RR 11-2018 Annex E, the weekly column, for a payslip of a weekly-paying company (`period.instalments >= 4`: the month’s four or five weeks): nothing to ₱4,808; 15% over 4,808; 432.60 + 20% over 7,692; 1,971.20 + 25% over 15,385; 7,740.45 + 30% over 38,462; 42,355.65 + 35% over 153,846 — the annual schedule over fifty-two, as the Annex prints it. The daily column is for a payroll paid every day, a cadence the runs do not offer. Applied 2026-09-23 (engine audit): the pools are the scheme's parts, never a company's codes — a class counting toward `WTAX.SPECIAL` is 13th-month pay and other benefits inside the PHP 90,000 pool, one counting toward `WTAX.RICE` the de minimis rice subsidy (`earned_average('WTAX.RICE', 0, 1)`, `earned_monthly_excess('WTAX.RICE', …)`); the salary the period attributes to `MATERNITY_LEAVE` days (`person.period.leave_pay`) is outside the base (RA 11210 s.5; RMC 105-2019). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): NIRC s.22(E)-(G), s.24(A) and s.25(A)-(B): a citizen and a resident alien, and a non-resident alien engaged in trade or business (one in the Philippines more than 180 days in the calendar year is deemed engaged, s.25(A)(1)), are withheld on the graduated table; a non-resident alien not engaged is withheld 25% of the gross (s.25(B)). The classification is `terms.tax_residency` (RESIDENT / NON_RESIDENT / NON_RESIDENT_NETB); the Code states no default for an unrecorded status, so positive taxable pay with none recorded stops the run. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test needs the floor the wage order fixes for the person (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(13)); where the version states none for the person's region and employment type (a kasambahay outside NCR), positive taxable pay stops the run instead of treating the person as above the floor. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): every de minimis benefit of RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3) as amended by RR 29-2025 (issued 22 December 2025, in force 6 January 2026) is its own class and WTAX part, each exempt to its ceiling and its excess an ‘other benefit’ inside the ₱90,000 exclusion: uniform `UNIFORM` ₱8,000, actual medical assistance `MEDICAL` ₱12,000, achievement awards `AWARD` ₱12,000, Christmas/anniversary gifts `GIFT` ₱6,000, CBA and productivity benefits combined `CBA` ₱12,000 — each a year, read against the year’s earlier payments; laundry `LAUNDRY` ₱400 a calendar month (as the rice subsidy); medical cash to dependants `DEP_MEDICAL` ₱2,000 a semester (January–June, July–December), read against the semester’s earlier payments; the overtime/night-shift meal allowance `OT_MEAL` is exempt to 30% of the regional basic minimum wage for each date with overtime or night-shift work. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5, V): RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(j) caps the exemption, not the pay — the class pays the keyed amount whole; the formula exempts 30% × minimum_wage(region) × 12 ÷ 313 × `person.period.overtime_days` of the part and pools the excess with the other benefits inside the ₱90,000 exclusion (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph; RMC 50-2018). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5, Z): RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph (restated by RMC 50-2018) counts de minimis benefits paid in excess of their ceilings among the 'other benefits' of the PHP 90,000 pool for the whole year, so an earlier payslip's excess of the overtime/night-shift meal allowance over its daily ceiling is 'earned before' too: `earned_daily_excess('WTAX.OT_MEAL', share of the monthly floor a day)` sums, month by month, the part less that share of the minimum wage each payslip was calculated at (the wage order then in force) times its overtime or night days.

rules.refusal: Record tax residency on the employment terms before calculating Philippine withholding: resident (citizen or resident alien), non-resident alien engaged in trade or business (graduated rates, NIRC s.25(A)), or not engaged (25% final, s.25(B)). The Tax Code states no default for an unknown status.

This version states no minimum wage for this employee's region and employment type (e.g. a kasambahay outside a transcribed domestic-worker wage order), so minimum-wage-earner status (NIRC s.24(A)(2), RR 11-2018) cannot be determined. Record the applicable wage order in the version before calculating withholding.

name: Social Security System
authority: RA 11199 ss.4(a)(9), 8(i), 9(a) and 18; SSS Circular 2024-006. Regular SS uses the first PHP20,000 monthly salary credit at 5% employee and 10% employer; excess to PHP35,000 belongs to SSS_MPF. Initial compulsory coverage extends through the 60th birthday. The first contribution liability date includes earlier employers and is independent of current registration. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/employees/ . Separation and retirement payments outside remuneration for services are excluded.

rules.refusal: SSS requires a birth date to determine statutory coverage.
SSS first contribution due date must be between birth and the assessment date.
SSS requires the first contribution due date, including earlier employers, to determine coverage.

name: SSS Mandatory Provident Fund (WISP)
authority: RA 11199 s.4(a)(2); SSS Circular 2024-006 II.B.2. Only a covered SSS member contributes to the Mandatory Provident Fund on salary credit above PHP20,000 through PHP35,000 at 5% employee and 10% employer. The Regular SS result establishes coverage, including the first-liability age test. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/pay-contribution/ .
assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + NIGHT_PREMIUM + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

The base is the BASIC line, which Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keeps whole against undertime, tardiness, leave without pay and absences (the ABSENCE and NO_PAY_LEAVE lines are not subtracted). Applied 2026-09-18: PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). Applied 2026-09-18: PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The base is the monthly basic salary whatever the pay frequency (`terms.monthly_basic`: a daily or hourly rate carried to the month by the person’s own factor). name: Withholding Tax on Compensation
authority: NIRC 1997 s.79 with s.24(A)(2)(a) as amended by RA 10963 (TRAIN), Revenue Regulations 11-2018 — revised withholding tax table effective 1 January 2023. The NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e) PHP 90,000 exemption for 13th-month pay is `annual_exempt(code('THIRTEENTH_MONTH_PAY'), year.earned.THIRTEENTH_MONTH_PAY, 90000.0)` in the formula. RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(d) as amended by RR 29-2025 (issued 22 December 2025, in force 6 January 2026): a rice subsidy of up to PHP 2,500 a month is a de minimis benefit outside compensation; the company's `meal` row is that subsidy (its sheet: "MEAL (RICE SUBSIDY)", with any excess booked as `allowance`), so the formula takes it out of the base up to PHP 30,000 a year — `annual_exempt(code('meal'), year.earned.meal, 30000.0)`, the monthly ceiling stated as its annual sum, exact for a level subsidy and reconciled by the year-end rung otherwise. The `bonus` allowance shares that ceiling and is not yet pooled with it (gap 105). The monthly and semi-monthly rungs relieve the SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG employee shares deducted in the same period (`produced.<code>.employee_this_period`, RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(B) as amended); only the year-end rung reads the year's shares. The SEMI-MONTHLY column (₱10,417 / 16,667 / 33,333 / 83,333 / 333,333; ₱937.50 / 4,270.70 / 16,770.70 / 91,770.70) governs a base paid in two instalments (`period.instalments == 2`); the MONTHLY column everything else. Applied 2026-09-18: RA 9504 (RR 11-2018): a statutory minimum-wage earner (basic at or below the region’s floor) is withheld on neither the basic wage, overtime, night shift differential nor holiday pay; the ₱90,000 exclusion is one pool across 13th-month pay and the bonus (NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e)); the de minimis meal allowance is exempt to 30% of the basic minimum wage (RR 29-2025); the MPF employee share relieves the taxable base beside the Regular SS share. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): NIRC s.32(B)(6)(a)–(b): retirement benefits under RA 7641 and separation pay for a cause beyond the employee’s control are excluded from gross income; s.24(A)(2) / RR 10-2008: a minimum wage earner’s statutory minimum wage, holiday pay, overtime pay and night shift differential are exempt (`person.wage_floor_pay`). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(13) / RR 10-2008: the exemption attaches to the pay for the days on which the employee is an MWE — the SMW is "the rate fixed by the RTWPB", which a wage order fixes from its effective date — so a month a wage order splits exempts the basic, overtime, holiday and night-differential pay of the days whose floor the rate is at or below and taxes the rest (`person.wage_floor_pay.<LINE>`: work-day lines by their date, the salary, leave and absence by the share of paid days). NCR September 2026: a ₱720 daily rate is above NCR-26’s ₱695 to 25 September (taxed) and at or below NCR-28’s ₱755 from 26 September (exempt). RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(d): the rice subsidy (the `meal` row) is de minimis to ₱2,000 a month, the excess taxable — a monthly figure, not a share of the annual minimum wage; the bonus is read once, through the 90,000 exemption, never also through the catalogue. The semi-monthly rung selector nets the MPF share with the SSS share. Applied 2026-09-19 (3): RR 11-2018 Annex E, the weekly column, for a payslip of a weekly-paying company (`period.instalments >= 4`: the month’s four or five weeks): nothing to ₱4,808; 15% over 4,808; 432.60 + 20% over 7,692; 1,971.20 + 25% over 15,385; 7,740.45 + 30% over 38,462; 42,355.65 + 35% over 153,846 — the annual schedule over fifty-two, as the Annex prints it. The daily column is for a payroll paid every day, a cadence the runs do not offer. Applied 2026-09-23 (engine audit): the pools are the scheme's parts, never a company's codes — a class counting toward `WTAX.SPECIAL` is 13th-month pay and other benefits inside the PHP 90,000 pool, one counting toward `WTAX.RICE` the de minimis rice subsidy (`earned_average('WTAX.RICE', 0, 1)`, `earned_monthly_excess('WTAX.RICE', …)`); the salary the period attributes to `MATERNITY_LEAVE` days (`person.period.leave_pay`) is outside the base (RA 11210 s.5; RMC 105-2019). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 3): this version opens on RR 29-2025’s commencement. RR 29-2025 s.3: in force fifteen days after publication on the BIR website (posted and stamped received 22 December 2025), i.e. 6 January 2026 — https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%2029-2025.pdf. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): NIRC s.22(E)-(G), s.24(A) and s.25(A)-(B): a citizen and a resident alien, and a non-resident alien engaged in trade or business (one in the Philippines more than 180 days in the calendar year is deemed engaged, s.25(A)(1)), are withheld on the graduated table; a non-resident alien not engaged is withheld 25% of the gross (s.25(B)). The classification is `terms.tax_residency` (RESIDENT / NON_RESIDENT / NON_RESIDENT_NETB); the Code states no default for an unrecorded status, so positive taxable pay with none recorded stops the run. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test needs the floor the wage order fixes for the person (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(13)); where the version states none for the person's region and employment type (a kasambahay outside NCR), positive taxable pay stops the run instead of treating the person as above the floor. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): every de minimis benefit of RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3) as amended by RR 29-2025 (issued 22 December 2025, in force 6 January 2026) is its own class and WTAX part, each exempt to its ceiling and its excess an ‘other benefit’ inside the ₱90,000 exclusion: uniform `UNIFORM` ₱8,000, actual medical assistance `MEDICAL` ₱12,000, achievement awards `AWARD` ₱12,000, Christmas/anniversary gifts `GIFT` ₱6,000, CBA and productivity benefits combined `CBA` ₱12,000 — each a year, read against the year’s earlier payments; laundry `LAUNDRY` ₱400 a calendar month (as the rice subsidy); medical cash to dependants `DEP_MEDICAL` ₱2,000 a semester (January–June, July–December), read against the semester’s earlier payments; the overtime/night-shift meal allowance `OT_MEAL` is exempt to 30% of the regional basic minimum wage for each date with overtime or night-shift work. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5, V): RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(j) caps the exemption, not the pay — the class pays the keyed amount whole; the formula exempts 30% × minimum_wage(region) × 12 ÷ 313 × `person.period.overtime_days` of the part and pools the excess with the other benefits inside the ₱90,000 exclusion (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph; RMC 50-2018). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5, Z): RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph (restated by RMC 50-2018) counts de minimis benefits paid in excess of their ceilings among the 'other benefits' of the PHP 90,000 pool for the whole year, so an earlier payslip's excess of the overtime/night-shift meal allowance over its daily ceiling is 'earned before' too: `earned_daily_excess('WTAX.OT_MEAL', share of the monthly floor a day)` sums, month by month, the part less that share of the minimum wage each payslip was calculated at (the wage order then in force) times its overtime or night days.

rules.refusal: Record tax residency on the employment terms before calculating Philippine withholding: resident (citizen or resident alien), non-resident alien engaged in trade or business (graduated rates, NIRC s.25(A)), or not engaged (25% final, s.25(B)). The Tax Code states no default for an unknown status.

This version states no minimum wage for this employee's region and employment type (e.g. a kasambahay outside a transcribed domestic-worker wage order), so minimum-wage-earner status (NIRC s.24(A)(2), RR 11-2018) cannot be determined. Record the applicable wage order in the version before calculating withholding.

name: Social Security System
authority: RA 11199 ss.4(a)(9), 8(i), 9(a) and 18; SSS Circular 2024-006. Regular SS uses the first PHP20,000 monthly salary credit at 5% employee and 10% employer; excess to PHP35,000 belongs to SSS_MPF. Initial compulsory coverage extends through the 60th birthday. The first contribution liability date includes earlier employers and is independent of current registration. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/employees/ . Separation and retirement payments outside remuneration for services are excluded.

rules.refusal: SSS requires a birth date to determine statutory coverage.
SSS first contribution due date must be between birth and the assessment date.
SSS requires the first contribution due date, including earlier employers, to determine coverage.

assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + NIGHT_PREMIUM + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: SSS Mandatory Provident Fund (WISP)
authority: RA 11199 s.4(a)(2); SSS Circular 2024-006 II.B.2. Only a covered SSS member contributes to the Mandatory Provident Fund on salary credit above PHP20,000 through PHP35,000 at 5% employee and 10% employer. The Regular SS result establishes coverage, including the first-liability age test. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/pay-contribution/ .
assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + NIGHT_PREMIUM + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: PhilHealth
authority: Republic Act 11223 (Universal Health Care Act) s.10 with PhilHealth Circular 2019-0009 and Advisory 2025-0002 — one 5% premium on the monthly basic salary, floor PHP 10,000, ceiling PHP 100,000, then split: employee = truncate_cent(premium / 2), employer = premium - employee (the published employer table; a half-centavo premium such as basic 15,819 -> 790.95 gives 395.47 / 395.48, not 395.48 twice). The base is the BASIC line, which Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keeps whole against undertime, tardiness, leave without pay and absences (the ABSENCE and NO_PAY_LEAVE lines are not subtracted). Applied 2026-09-18: PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). Applied 2026-09-18: PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The base is the monthly basic salary whatever the pay frequency (`terms.monthly_basic`: a daily or hourly rate carried to the month by the person’s own factor). RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.30: where a domestic worker earns less than ₱5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium — the employee share is zero and the employer carries both.

Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The base is the monthly basic salary whatever the pay frequency (`terms.monthly_basic`: a daily or hourly rate carried to the month by the person’s own factor). RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.30: where a domestic worker earns less than ₱5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium — the employee share is zero and the employer carries both.

name: Withholding Tax on Compensation
authority: NIRC 1997 s.79 with s.24(A)(2)(a) as amended by RA 10963 (TRAIN), Revenue Regulations 11-2018 — revised withholding tax table effective 1 January 2023. The NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e) PHP 90,000 exemption for 13th-month pay is `annual_exempt(code('THIRTEENTH_MONTH_PAY'), year.earned.THIRTEENTH_MONTH_PAY, 90000.0)` in the formula. RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(d) as amended by RR 29-2025 (issued 22 December 2025, in force 6 January 2026): a rice subsidy of up to PHP 2,500 a month is a de minimis benefit outside compensation; the company's `meal` row is that subsidy (its sheet: "MEAL (RICE SUBSIDY)", with any excess booked as `allowance`), so the formula takes it out of the base up to PHP 30,000 a year — `annual_exempt(code('meal'), year.earned.meal, 30000.0)`, the monthly ceiling stated as its annual sum, exact for a level subsidy and reconciled by the year-end rung otherwise. The `bonus` allowance shares that ceiling and is not yet pooled with it (gap 105). The monthly and semi-monthly rungs relieve the SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG employee shares deducted in the same period (`produced.<code>.employee_this_period`, RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(B) as amended); only the year-end rung reads the year's shares. The SEMI-MONTHLY column (₱10,417 / 16,667 / 33,333 / 83,333 / 333,333; ₱937.50 / 4,270.70 / 16,770.70 / 91,770.70) governs a base paid in two instalments (`period.instalments == 2`); the MONTHLY column everything else. Applied 2026-09-18: RA 9504 (RR 11-2018): a statutory minimum-wage earner (basic at or below the region’s floor) is withheld on neither the basic wage, overtime, night shift differential nor holiday pay; the ₱90,000 exclusion is one pool across 13th-month pay and the bonus (NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e)); the de minimis meal allowance is exempt to 30% of the basic minimum wage (RR 29-2025); the MPF employee share relieves the taxable base beside the Regular SS share. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): NIRC s.32(B)(6)(a)–(b): retirement benefits under RA 7641 and separation pay for a cause beyond the employee’s control are excluded from gross income; s.24(A)(2) / RR 10-2008: a minimum wage earner’s statutory minimum wage, holiday pay, overtime pay and night shift differential are exempt (`person.wage_floor_pay`). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(13) / RR 10-2008: the exemption attaches to the pay for the days on which the employee is an MWE — the SMW is "the rate fixed by the RTWPB", which a wage order fixes from its effective date — so a month a wage order splits exempts the basic, overtime, holiday and night-differential pay of the days whose floor the rate is at or below and taxes the rest (`person.wage_floor_pay.<LINE>`: work-day lines by their date, the salary, leave and absence by the share of paid days). NCR September 2026: a ₱720 daily rate is above NCR-26’s ₱695 to 25 September (taxed) and at or below NCR-28’s ₱755 from 26 September (exempt). RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(d): the rice subsidy (the `meal` row) is de minimis to ₱2,000 a month, the excess taxable — a monthly figure, not a share of the annual minimum wage; the bonus is read once, through the 90,000 exemption, never also through the catalogue. The semi-monthly rung selector nets the MPF share with the SSS share. Applied 2026-09-19 (3): RR 11-2018 Annex E, the weekly column, for a payslip of a weekly-paying company (`period.instalments >= 4`: the month’s four or five weeks): nothing to ₱4,808; 15% over 4,808; 432.60 + 20% over 7,692; 1,971.20 + 25% over 15,385; 7,740.45 + 30% over 38,462; 42,355.65 + 35% over 153,846 — the annual schedule over fifty-two, as the Annex prints it. The daily column is for a payroll paid every day, a cadence the runs do not offer. Applied 2026-09-23 (engine audit): the pools are the scheme's parts, never a company's codes — a class counting toward `WTAX.SPECIAL` is 13th-month pay and other benefits inside the PHP 90,000 pool, one counting toward `WTAX.RICE` the de minimis rice subsidy (`earned_average('WTAX.RICE', 0, 1)`, `earned_monthly_excess('WTAX.RICE', …)`); the salary the period attributes to `MATERNITY_LEAVE` days (`person.period.leave_pay`) is outside the base (RA 11210 s.5; RMC 105-2019). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 3): this version opens on RR 29-2025’s commencement. RR 29-2025 s.3: in force fifteen days after publication on the BIR website (posted and stamped received 22 December 2025), i.e. 6 January 2026 — https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%2029-2025.pdf. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): NIRC s.22(E)-(G), s.24(A) and s.25(A)-(B): a citizen and a resident alien, and a non-resident alien engaged in trade or business (one in the Philippines more than 180 days in the calendar year is deemed engaged, s.25(A)(1)), are withheld on the graduated table; a non-resident alien not engaged is withheld 25% of the gross (s.25(B)). The classification is `terms.tax_residency` (RESIDENT / NON_RESIDENT / NON_RESIDENT_NETB); the Code states no default for an unrecorded status, so positive taxable pay with none recorded stops the run. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test needs the floor the wage order fixes for the person (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(13)); where the version states none for the person's region and employment type (a kasambahay outside NCR), positive taxable pay stops the run instead of treating the person as above the floor. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): every de minimis benefit of RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3) as amended by RR 29-2025 (issued 22 December 2025, in force 6 January 2026) is its own class and WTAX part, each exempt to its ceiling and its excess an ‘other benefit’ inside the ₱90,000 exclusion: uniform `UNIFORM` ₱8,000, actual medical assistance `MEDICAL` ₱12,000, achievement awards `AWARD` ₱12,000, Christmas/anniversary gifts `GIFT` ₱6,000, CBA and productivity benefits combined `CBA` ₱12,000 — each a year, read against the year’s earlier payments; laundry `LAUNDRY` ₱400 a calendar month (as the rice subsidy); medical cash to dependants `DEP_MEDICAL` ₱2,000 a semester (January–June, July–December), read against the semester’s earlier payments; the overtime/night-shift meal allowance `OT_MEAL` is exempt to 30% of the regional basic minimum wage for each date with overtime or night-shift work. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5, V): RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3)(j) caps the exemption, not the pay — the class pays the keyed amount whole; the formula exempts 30% × minimum_wage(region) × 12 ÷ 313 × `person.period.overtime_days` of the part and pools the excess with the other benefits inside the ₱90,000 exclusion (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph; RMC 50-2018). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5, Z): RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph (restated by RMC 50-2018) counts de minimis benefits paid in excess of their ceilings among the 'other benefits' of the PHP 90,000 pool for the whole year, so an earlier payslip's excess of the overtime/night-shift meal allowance over its daily ceiling is 'earned before' too: `earned_daily_excess('WTAX.OT_MEAL', share of the monthly floor a day)` sums, month by month, the part less that share of the minimum wage each payslip was calculated at (the wage order then in force) times its overtime or night days.
